extracted.intended_audience: horror/dark-fantasy authors, publishers, and HWA members preparing or considering submissions to the Bram Stoker Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and eligibility rules for submitting or recommending horror and dark‑fantasy works to the Horror Writers Association's Bram Stoker Awards, including category fit, publication timing, recommendation/voting rules, formats, deadlines, and judging considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Year Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must have been published in the last calendar year to be considered. Works must be published in the year preceding the awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the awards reflect the latest in horror literature. The page also notes a submission-time exception/clarification for late-year publications (see Deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Recommendations for Preliminary Ballot
rubrics_metrics.description: A work needs at least five member recommendations to make the preliminary ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are required from HWA members for a work to appear on the preliminary ballot; reaching the five‑recommendation threshold is a concrete eligibility requirement before jury/ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Recommend vs. Who Can Vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Many (anyone) can suggest or recommend works, but only Active and Lifetime HWA members can vote on nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may suggest works (wider community participation), but formal voting privilege is limited to HWA Active and Lifetime members. The page also repeatedly refers to Active members as the voting cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting Eligibility / Member Voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Active HWA members can vote on nominations; HWA members participate in recommending and voting processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasises the role of the roughly 1,600+ HWA members in seeing and voting on titles; being visible to members increases chances of being recommended and voted on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Fit / Specific Categories for Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be entered in the correct Bram Stoker Award category (e.g., Superior Achievement in a Novel, First Novel, Graphic Novel, Young Adult Novel, Long Fiction, Short Fiction, Anthology, Fiction Collection, Poetry Collection, Non-Fiction, Short Non-Fiction, Screenplay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the correct category is essential — different formats and career stages are recognized separately (e.g., First Novel vs. Best Novel). Make sure your work aligns with the category definitions used by HWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Works and Formats Accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible works include novels, short stories, graphic novels, poetry collections, non‑fiction works, fiction collections, anthologies, and screenplays; acceptable formats include print publications, digital formats, and online publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your work is one of the accepted types and in an acceptable format; the awards accept both print and digital/online publications so long as they meet availability/distribution expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and Accessibility Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For a work to be considered, it must be easily accessible — available in print, digital, or online formats and have sufficient reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication's reach and availability to readers (and HWA members) is important to eligibility; works should be available to a wide enough audience to be reviewable by members and jurors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Platform and Required Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be uploaded through Submittable with all required information and documents. Digital copies are preferred; hard copies are usually not accepted unless no digital option exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission instructions carefully on Submittable (titles, links, documentation). The page advises uploading digital copies where possible and including helpful links to where the work can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Special Timing Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard submission deadline: 11:59 PM Pacific Standard Time on November 30 each year. If a work is published between December 1 and December 31, you have until December 31 to submit. Member recommendations are open until January 15 of the next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track these specific dates (submission cutoff, late‑December publication allowance, and recommendation window). The page stresses not waiting until the last minute and being mindful of the different windows for submission versus member recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Ballot Formation and Nomination Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Member recommendations produce a preliminary ballot (works need the five‑recommendation threshold). Jurors then rank their top picks; the top five in the preliminary ballot move on to the final ballot/nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process involves community recommendations followed by juror ranking. Understanding this two‑stage process (recommendations → preliminary ballot → juror ranking → final ballot) is key to anticipating how nominations are selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Criteria — Quality Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurors and judges evaluate works primarily on originality, creativity, and how well the work fits the horror/dark fantasy genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is subjective and jurors make independent decisions; emphasis is on strong, original writing and clear genre alignment. The page suggests that appealing to a range of readers and jurors can help a work stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominee Recognition / Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees receive a Certificate and are listed on the HWA website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being nominated brings visibility and formal recognition from HWA; the article frames nomination benefits as part of why meeting eligibility and submission standards matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies to Improve Chances
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips include following submission guidelines carefully, submitting early (don’t wait until the deadline), networking with HWA members, and aiming to get on the Recommended Reading list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are non‑binding strategies rather than formal rules: follow technical requirements exactly, make your work visible to HWA members, and use early submission to allow time for review and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Reach as an Eligibility Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication’s reach is emphasized as a factor for eligibility — works should be available to many people to meet awards' standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a strict numeric threshold, the article implies that limited‑circulation or inaccessible publications may not meet the spirit of the accessibility requirement; aim for distribution that allows members and jurors to read the work.
